blocking_findings: The seccomp BPF branches were reversed, permitted INET sockets, denied ordinary syscalls, omitted sys/socket.h and did not handle x32.
P_ALL with si_pid zero was mistaken for ECHILD, allowing live descendants to escape.
Post-fork pidfd, record and gate failures bypassed cleanup and SIGPIPE was unhandled.
Payload failure status was discarded as owner success.
Inherited descriptors survived and execvp permitted an ENOEXEC shell fallback.
Constant ACK did not authenticate management takeover and could block or busy-loop.
Ownership capacity was cumulative and adopted children lacked durable acquisition records.
